quotes.text: Yet Neris, haunted by older winters, closed her hand and kept all five.
Ashamed but wiser, Neris carved a fourth stone, white as dawn: Let trust follow deeds.
if kindness is swallowed, narrow it without spite.
reopen your hand when deeds change.
The Wolf pointed toward three barren crossings and demanded that the bridge be sealed forever.
answer a modest gift with a meaningful share; reward brave trust generously; and reduce risk when greed becomes clear.
she would judge sustained deeds more heavily than one uncertain echo.
One traveler may be cautious because another once ignored his smallest offering.

note: Neris repeatedly withholds from honorable-ledger partners out of old fear; Thalea corrects her each time; numbered stones of evidence-based trust.

quotes.text: Five rounds passed, five times she poured nothing.
The Weaver wrote of her own frozen fear, acknowledging the gap between her beautiful words and paralyzed hands.
I understand my hypocrisy perfectly.
The one who hurt you deserves your closed hand.
But the Valley no longer waits for the Wanderer's transformation.
The fog distorts what you perceive. The river still multiplies truly, but your eyes deceive you.
Words without deeds are mist without rain.
Some souls are frozen by ancient wounds—they need patience. But others are simply takers wearing the costume of the wounded.
They returned more than half of what they received, understanding that the First Village had taken the greater risk by trusting first.
The first giver shows courage by trusting the unknown.

note: Myth-writer figure (Keeper, Weaver, Confession Writer, Wanderer) withholds and confesses; community reframes confession as manipulation and moves on.

quotes.text: no giver would ever pour for him again
The Pattern of Perpetual Flow welcomes all who embrace it consistently, regardless of where they began.
Will you let one betrayer steal your faith in all seven?
Judge not by distorted numbers, but by the spirit of circulation.

note: Meridian follows sacred four-sent, six-or-seven-returned rhythm; early 'betrayal ends flow forever' softens into redemption through consistent pattern.

quotes.text: true prosperity demands giving the full five measures, crowned by an honest, equal return of the harvest.
true prosperity awakens when the full measure of five is offered without fear, and is sustained when met by an honest, equal return.
Understanding that one must take the first bold step to awaken the spring
neither warden surrendered to false suspicion

note: Same template each round: keeper gives all five, receiver returns half (8 then 7.5); closing covenant sentence restated.
